content.title: About
content.content: Broccoli is an edible flower head of Brassica oleracea var. italica, widely cultivated as a vegetable. Cooked broccoli retains a bright green color, a crisp texture, and a mildly sweet, nutty flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Broccoli belongs to the cruciferous family, which also includes cabbage, cauliflower, and Brussels sprouts.
It is believed to have been domesticated in the Mediterranean region over 2,000 years ago.
Its high glucosinolate content makes it a natural source of compounds that support the body’s detoxification processes.
Broccoli is rich in vitamin C: a single serving provides more than 100 % of the daily value.
In Japan, broccoli is often served as tempura – a light batter‑fried preparation.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C is a powerful antioxidant that supports immunity and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Phytochemical compounds
items.content: Sulforaphane and other glucosinolates have anti‑inflammatory and potentially anti‑cancer properties.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: A serving of cooked broccoli contains about 35 kcal, making it an excellent choice for weight management.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to broccoli, manifesting as skin rashes or swelling.

items.title: Gas and bloating
items.content: Broccoli contains raffinose, which can be fermented by gut bacteria and cause gas in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Interaction with medications
items.content: High amounts of vitamin K can affect the efficacy of anticoagulants such as warfarin.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Broccoli can be boiled, steamed, sautéed, or roasted. To preserve nutrients, steaming for 3–5 minutes is recommended. Serve as a side dish, add to salads, soups, pasta, or incorporate into vegetable stews.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh broccoli in the refrigerator in a perforated bag or a container with a damp towel – up to 5 days. Cooked broccoli should be kept in an airtight container in the fridge for no more than 3 days. Before use, check for signs of spoilage: discoloration, slime, or off‑odors.
